Subject: Acme Health - model fit & streaming UX follow-up

Hi Emma - thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

Summary of discovery:
- Primary product use: real-time transcription + on-device summary for telehealth visits (average length 6-12 minutes).
- Top constraints: 99th-percentile latency < 250ms per response chunk, stop-sequence fidelity for clinical notes, and strict PII redaction.
- Volume: ~1200 sessions/day initially, ramping to ~8k/day in year 1.

Model fit & initial recommendations:
- For draft evals we recommend running two variants: redwood-stream-v1 (higher coherence in streaming) and redwood-compact-q4 (cost-optimized quantized baseline).
- Suggested eval suite: conversation-level ROUGE / clinical entity F1, hallucination checklist, and streaming partial-output coherence metric (we've shared a sample harness below).

Attachments and links:
- I attached the prompt set we discussed (acme_prompt_set_v1.json) and a starter eval harness for streaming. Also see benchmarks: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-health

Immediate next steps (action owners):
1) Redwood: run a 1k-session eval with both model variants and return streaming trace + latency histogram (Jordan + Vivek) - target by Nov 30.
2) Acme: share 50 de-identified transcripts and the critical stop-sequences you need enforced (Emma) - target Nov 27.
3) Procurement: Emma to escalate pricing visibility and any PO constraints (Tom).

Would you be available for a 30m sync next Tuesday (Nov 30) to review results and agree on a small canary?

Thanks - looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emma Chen <emma.chen@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Acme Health - model fit & streaming UX follow-up

Hi Emma - quick technical follow-up on the two variants and stop-sequence handling (high level):

1) redwood-stream-v1:
- Streaming-first model: incremental decoding with partial token emission; improved prefix coherence via attention caching.
- Stop-sequence enforcement: we apply a best-effort immediate check at the tokenizer boundary for each emitted chunk and a final pass at chunk completion. This reduces false positives but can still emit trailing tokens if a stop token aligns mid-token.
- Suggested mitigations: use explicit sentinel tokens in prompts (e.g., "<END_CLINICAL_NOTE>") and include a short trailing guard prompt like "\n<END_CLINICAL_NOTE>\n" on the final prompt line to encourage clean termination.

2) redwood-compact-q4:
- Quantized variant optimized for cost; deterministic decoding is slightly noisier in streaming, so we don't recommend it for first-pass clinical notes. Good for batch summarization fallback.

Prompt templates & eval artifacts I've attached: acme_prompt_set_v1.json and a first-pass streaming evaluation we ran against 200 synthetic transcripts (streaming_eval_results.csv). Key notes from the run:
- redwood-stream-v1: mean per-chunk latency 110ms, p95 320ms at our test rig (single-region, simulated 2k concurrent streams).
- We observed partial-output coherence issues in ~3.6% of segments tied to very long utterances (>40 tokens) where the model produced an unfinished clause that later resolved once more tokens arrived.

Next steps I propose:
- We'll run the 1k-session eval with your de-identified transcripts and include a focused check on stop-sequence fidelity and partial-output duplication.
- We'll also instrument a stronger end-of-stream enforcement for the canary: post-process emitted stream buffer to strip trailing unmatched partial tokens (this is a conservative safety net).

I'll drop the synthetic eval CSV into the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-acme-eval

-Jordan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

From: Emma Chen <emma.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Acme Health - model fit & streaming UX follow-up

Thanks Jordan - that clarifies the mechanisms. We ran a quick internal pass on 12 transcripts (sanitized) and are seeing two concrete issues to flag for the 1k eval:

1) Partial output duplication: when network jitter caused small re-transmits, our client-side reassembly saw identical partial fragments twice in ~1.8% of segments. Would be great to see server-side idempotency markers in stream chunks to help client dedupe.
2) Stop-sequence jitter: in 4 of 12 samples the exact sentinel string was split across two chunks which resulted in a failure to terminate; client currently depends on exact match.

I attached our lightweight test harness output (streaming_eval_results.csv) and included a short log snippet in the CSV.

As an ask for the canary: could you include a mode that emits per-chunk sequence numbers and a short checksum that clients can use to verify chunk completeness? That will make our parsing much simpler and safe.

Also, re: latency - at scale our SLO target is p95 < 250ms; your p95 of 320ms in the synthetic run is a concern unless we can tighten it via batching knobs or smaller chunk sizes.

-Emma

- Procurement (Tom): we can provide a preliminary canary pricing addendum; Marissa will send an initial SOW & PO template.

I'll schedule a 30m review for Friday Dec 3 at 10:00am PT unless you prefer another time - please confirm.

Action items assigned in-line. If all good I'll also spin up a short internal runbook for the canary to make rollback safe.

Marissa
